title: Jacobi-Zariski sequence is exact on the left when the last map is a regular-sequence quotient
statement: Let $A\to B\xrightarrow{\ \varphi\ }C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, $C$ an $A$-algebra through the composite. Assume there are integers $m,c\ge0$, elements $f_1,\dots,f_c$ of the polynomial ring $B[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] which form a regular sequence in $B[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and a surjective homomorphism of $B$-algebras $\beta:B[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to C$ whose kernel is the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. For a ring map $R\to S$ let $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}=\bigl(I_{S/R}/I_{S/R}^2\xrightarrow{\delta_{S/R}}\bigoplus_{s\in S}S\,\mathrm d[s]\bigr)$ be the naive cotangent complex of the canonical presentation $R[S]\to S$, $[s]\mapsto s$, with kernel $I_{S/R}$, and $H_1(L_{S/R})=\ker\delta_{S/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Let $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)$ be the kernel of $\delta_{B/A}\otimes\mathrm{id}_C:I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}^2\otimes_BC\to\bigoplus_{b\in B}C\,\mathrm d[b]$, and let $\varphi_\sharp:A[B]\to A[C]$ be the $A$-algebra map $[b]\mapsto[\varphi(b)]$. Then the $C$-linear map $I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}^2\otimes_BC\to I_{C/A}/I_{C/A}^2$, $(g\bmod I_{B/A}^2)\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot(\varphi_\sharp(g)\bmod I_{C/A}^2)$, maps $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)$ into $H_1(L_{C/A})$, and its restriction $u:H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)\to H_1(L_{C/A})$ is injective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07D4 (lemma-transitive-lci-at-end, line 8459), its 'in particular' clause (the six-term sequence of Algebra Lemma 00S2 completed with a zero on the left), for B -> C presented by a regular sequence: a regular sequence is Koszul-regular (More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 062F, lemma-regular-koszul-regular, line 7265), so B -> C is a local complete intersection in the sense of More on Algebra, Definition Tag 07D0 (definition-local-complete-intersection, line 8338). Proof of 07D4 (lines 8494-8505) uses Lemma Tag 07CX (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular-ideal, line 8235). Tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags.

proof.text: Construct Q=Generators.ofAlgHom beta hBeta, P=Generators.self A B and T=Q.comp P. Extensionality shows Q.ker=Ideal.ofList fs. The coefficient map q=(Q.ofComp P).toAlgHom is surjective and maps T.ker to Q.ker; its kernel is contained in T.ker by compatibility of the two evaluation maps.

Lift each member of fs through q. Every lift lies in T.ker, since any difference from a lift in T.ker is in ker q. The first isomorphism theorem identifies T/ker q with Q.Ring. Transport regularity using AddEquiv.isRegular_congr and the multiplication compatibility, and transport Ideal.ofList along the same equivalence. Apply inf_sq_eq_mul_of_regular_quotient to obtain ker q intersect T.ker² = ker q * T.ker. These steps are the proved private intersection_of_surjective_regular helper.

Apply the composed-conormal injectivity lemma to Q and P with the identity from step 2. The cotangent differential square commutes by Mathlib Generators.H1Cotangent.map_comp_cotangentComplex_baseChange. Hence the conormal map restricts to r:ker(P.cotangentComplex.baseChange C)->T.H1Cotangent. Injectivity of the ambient map implies injectivity of r.

Compose r with Mathlib Generators.H1Cotangent.equiv T (Generators.self A C). To verify the requested ambient equation, compose the conormal maps and compare the resulting presentation hom j.comp i with the canonical default hom f. Mathlib Cotangent.map_sub_map expresses their difference as a map composed with the differential; after base change its value on a kernel element is zero. Thus the two ambient maps agree on the kernel. Equality under the composite implies equality under r by the comparison equivalence, then equality of the original kernel elements by ambient conormal injectivity and Subtype.ext.

split_report.summary: Stacks 07D4 specialized to the given regular-sequence presentation: form T=A[B][y] and its ideals I_T and K; use the new restricted 07CX node to get I_T cap K^2=I_T K, identify (I/I^2) tensor_B C with I_T/(I_T K), and thus inject the conormal module into K/K^2; use 00S1 presentation functoriality to compare H_1 of gamma with the canonical presentation and check the resulting map is the specified u. Statement unchanged. One new unsplit node, conormal intersection for a regular-sequence quotient. Mathlib has the Jacobi-Zariski sequence through H_1 but no left injectivity in this generality.

lean.statement: theorem jacobiZariski_left_injective_of_regularSequence (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (C : Type w) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C] (m : ℕ) (fs : List (MvPolynomial (Fin m) B)) (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (MvPolynomial (Fin m) B) fs) (β : MvPolynomial (Fin m) B →ₐ[B] C) (hβ : Function.Surjective β) (hker : RingHom.ker β.toRingHom = Ideal.ofList fs) : let P := (Generators.self A B).toExtension let Q := (Generators.self A C).toExtension let F := (Generators.defaultHom (Generators.self A B) (Generators.self A C)).toExtensionHom let d := P.cotangentComplex.baseChange C let g := (Extension.Cotangent.map F).liftBaseChange C ∃ u : LinearMap.ker d →ₗ[C] H1Cotangent A C, (∀ x : LinearMap.ker d, Q.h1Cotangentι (u x) = g x.1) ∧ Function.Injective u

reviewed_lean.note: A->B->C as Algebra A B, Algebra B C, Algebra A C + IsScalarTower; f_i as List over MvPolynomial (Fin m) B with RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (weakly regular + top_ne_smul = M/(f)M != 0); beta B-alg hom, surjective, ker = Ideal.ofList fs; NL via Generators.self (val=id, sigma=X), H1Cotangent A C rfl to Q.H1Cotangent; phi_sharp = defaultHom, val b = X (algebraMap B C b) by rfl; g = Cotangent.map F liftBaseChange C (c (x) x -> c . map x, map_mk = phi_sharp(g) mod I^2); d = cotangentComplex.baseChange C, ker d = H1(NL_{B/A} (x) C) without flatness; exists u with h1Cotangentii (u x) = g x and Injective u = maps-into + restriction injective; no hollow hyps, no test-object universes
